body: After Nc4, White's knight on c4 controls d6; after Nb1, White's knight on b1 does not control d6. In the provided Nb1 line, the same knight next moves with Nc3 to c3. After Nef6, White's knight on c4 controls d6. After Nc4 Nef6, Rd6 remains competitive alongside Ra7 here. A leading tested reply to Rd6 is Qc7. After Qc7, Black's queen on c7 keeps targeting White's rook on d6. Qc7 moves the queen out of the attack from White's rook on d6. After Nef6, White's knight on b1 does not control d6. After Nb1 Nef6, prefer Nc3 to an immediate Rd6. A leading tested reply to Rd6 is Qxd6. Nc4 adds knight control of d6. In the legal variation Nc4 Nef6 Rd6 Qxd6, White can recapture with Nxd6. After Nb1 Nef6 Rd6 Qxd6, that capture with the same knight is unavailable. The recorded continuation is Nc4. The recorded continuation is Nb1. In the Nc4 line: Qxd6 captures the white rook on d6. Nxd6 recaptures the black queen on d6. In the Nb1 line: Qxd6 captures the white rook on d6. The compared root choices are Nc4 and Nb1. Nb1 clears d2; Qd2 later occupies that square in this line. After Qd2, White's queen on d2 now targets Black's knight on d7. In the Nc4 line: After Rd6, White's rook on d6 now targets Black's queen on c6 and Black's knight on f6, and keeps targeting Black's knight on d7. Nc4 clears d2; later Rd6 passes through that square in this line. Separately, in the recorded Nc4 Nef6 Rd6 Qc7 Rad1 b5 continuation: Nxd6 captures the white rook on d6. Bxb7 captures the black queen on b7. In the Nc4 line: Rd6 clears d1; Rad1 later occupies that square in this line. Nc4 clears d2; later Rad1 uses the cleared line to target White's rook on d6 in this line. After Rad1, White's rook on d1 adds support to White's rook on d6, which is under attack from Black's queen on c7.
